sources.entry: FileBrowser Quantum | Actively maintained FileBrowser fork with search, sharing and OIDC

summary.one_liner: FileBrowser Quantum is a self-hosted, web-based file manager and a fork of the original FileBrowser project, with multi-source configuration, search, sharing, and OIDC/LDAP login.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a web file manager with a responsive interface for managing users, access, sharing, file preview, and editing. It is configured through a config.yaml file and supports multiple sources with include/exclude rules. Login options listed are OIDC, LDAP, JWT, password with 2FA, and proxy authentication. Search is described as real-time as you type, with filters for file and folder sizes, and the UI updates live as files change. Thumbnails are said to cover office documents, video, album artwork, and 3D models, and folder sizes are displayed. Sharing supports expiration times, access for anonymous or named users, and styling, and access control can be scoped per user, group, or source path. It also offers WebDAV support, long-lived API tokens, and a Swagger page at /swagger. The README states that shell command execution was removed from this fork.
use_cases: self-hosted file browser in a web browser
share files with others via expiring links
web-based file manager with LDAP or OIDC login
search across files on a home server
manage user access to folders on a server
preview and edit files in the browser
how_to_run: See the Official Docs (Getting Started) referenced in the README; no install commands are given in the README text provided
stack: Go (implied by the FileBrowser lineage; not stated in the README)
notable: Multiple sources with include/exclude rules, configured in config.yaml
Real-time search and live UI updates as files change
Thumbnails for office files, video, album art, and 3D models
Long-lived API tokens and a Swagger API page
Ships as a standalone binary, per its comparison chart
caveats: README says a stable release is planned, though it also marks v2.0.0 as stable
Shell commands were removed from this fork
Some comparison-table features (chat, tags, notifications, metrics, trash, archive browsing) are marked as work in progress
